5.1 LONG-LEAD EQUIPMENT PROCUREMENT

Based on the project scope, the lone long-lead piece of equipment is considered to be pre-engineered modular E-house. In order to be more cost effective, Tetra Tech has considered that a Technical Specification will be produced, detailing the critical performance and functional requirements of the e- house, as well as the applicable Codes to which it needs to be designed and fabricated.

The Technical Specification will be drafted at the 30% design stage and will include the elements of the e-house, including the architectural, structural, mechanical (i.e., HVAC and fire protection systems), electrical (i.e., 600VAC, 120VAC, lighting, emergency lighting, ventilation power) and Instrumentation / Control system (i.e., PA and fire detection).

Upon OPG acceptance at the 60% design stage, this will be tendered to local (Southern Ontario) fabricators. If OPG has a preferred vendor, this will be considered during the tendering process.

Once a vendor has been selected and a Purchase Order issued to them, they will produce drawings for Tetra Tech's review. The review will be conducted in accordance with the Technical Specifications and specific project requirements. Once drawings are accepted, they will be incorporated into the 100% Design Package for OPG review.

Funds will also be released to the vendor to initiate procurement and fabrication of the e-house.

Tetra Tech will provide a biweekly report outlining work performed during the reporting period, planned activities for the next reporting period, and updates on engineering progress, vendor document reviews, FAT status, action list, and issues/challenges, etc.

Tetra Tech QMS has an integrated document control system that ensures all documents are uniquely identified, tracked, and are revision controlled.

Tetra Tech uses a Document ID Control System (DICS) to generate unique document numbers for all HYDRO ONE generated documents as a way of ensuring easy traceability and maintaining control on all project-related documents. Document Control (DC) personnel ensure all documents issued contain a proper document ID number and verify the number exists on the DICS. All Tetra Tech document control personnel fully understand the HYDRO ONE Drawing & Document Requirements and process per previous experiences.

Control of Outgoing Document to B&M

Document control will use project schedules and identified milestone dates to manage outgoing deliverables.

When transmitting files to Document Control, project personnel will provide clear instruction and information in their email and save all documents to be submitted, along with their native files, to the Project's 'Doc Control/To Be Issued' folder.

The document control coordinator will perform a standard quality check (QC) on all documents to ensure that applicable criteria are met. If the criteria is not met, the documents will be sent back to the submitter to be corrected. As a guideline, Tetra Tech document control use Internal QC Checklists. Once the QC checks have been completed document control will issue the documents and save an electronic copy of the QC checklist in a subfolder titled 'TT document control QC' within the same folder as the submitted documents.

If documents are provided in hard copy, document control will scan and save them along with any electronic files to the appropriate folder under Doc Control/Outgoing Docs. If document numbers are required or revisions need to be updated, the document control coordinator will do so using the DICS and rename the file using the new document number. Prior to issuing documents, document control will update the project's "Master List of Deliverables" if applicable, to reflect the new status and date of issue for all documents being transmitted.

2.0 SCOPE OF WORK UNDERSTANDING

Tetra Tech understands that due to the impact of the other projects currently underway, it is required that Wallaceburg TS to be converted to 230 kV. A feasibility study was completed for the Wallaceburg TS 230 kV conversion in 2022, and it was concluded that the existing two (2) 25/33/42 MVA 115 kV/ 27.6 kV transformers can be replaced with two (2) 230 kV/ 27.6 kV transformers within existing station property.
